purpose: Reproduce the owner's 'extra border on menubar popups' (U1) in Chromium against the ordinary Vite route (mock bridge), and identify the mechanism.
engine: Playwright Chromium 1228 (headless), viewport 1280x800, http://127.0.0.1:4199/ served by `npm run dev` (bridge mock). Not the native WebKit binary.

results.label: 1 fresh load, pointer click About
results.activeElement: DIV.overflow radixOverflow aboutMenu (the Radix menu content)

results.label: 2 after a pointer click in the page, About again
5 fresh reload, keyboard Enter on focused File trigger
6b About after opening Settings by pointer

mechanism: frontend/src/ui/styles/base.css:104-107 applies `*:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); outline: 0 }` to every element. A pointer-opened Radix DropdownMenu.Content (File/About in ShellMenuRow, View in ViewMenu) becomes document.activeElement and matches :focus-visible in Chromium, so the global rule REPLACES the popup's `box-shadow: var(--win-shadow)` (ShellMenuRow.module.css:99, MenuSurface.module.css:69). Result: a 2px+4px accent ring and no drop shadow, exactly as in the owner's screenshots owner-popup-about.png and owner-popup-view-before.png. Keyboard opening focuses the first item instead, so the container keeps its shadow.
themeDependence: Not a theme bug. In Chromium the ring appears on every pointer open regardless of theme interaction. The owner's native WebKit observation (ring at startup, gone after a theme change) is consistent with WebKit's :focus-visible heuristic for programmatically focused elements, which depends on the most recent input modality; it was not reproduced natively here (native screenshots unavailable).
fix_direction: Scope the focus ring to interactive controls (or exclude role=menu containers / use outline instead of box-shadow so it composes with the surface shadow), in ONE shared popup surface used by every menu family; verify with a computed-style assertion on pointer-opened menus.
